title: Bipartisan Backlash Hits Sam Altman Over AI Risk Comments
summary:
U.S. legislators from both parties and industry executives have condemned OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for arguing that society must tolerate specific harms to advance artificial intelligence. Senator Bernie Sanders questioned if these failures included mass extinction or a global financial crisis and called for an immediate pause on development. House Agriculture Committee Chair GT Thompson, citing his 28 year career in healthcare, rejected the trade off, while Republican opponents in Florida labeled the stance as recklessness.

The controversy stems from a Politico interview where Altman suggested that the risk of AI scams and misuse is a necessary cost to prevent a few labs from gatekeeping the technology. Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry disputed the logic, asserting that any abnormal results are unacceptable and advocating for more rigorous testing over slower deployment. While Altman draws a line at catastrophic risks like a total loss of human control, he continues to advocate for a lighter touch regulatory environment than the one proposed by Anthropic.

ALTMAN: WORLD SHOULD ACCEPT SOME AI RISKS

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says “the world should accept some bad things happening” to keep AI broadly accessible, arguing that people will ultimately use the technology for far more good than harm.

Altman drew the line at catastrophic risks such as severe loss of control, while arguing that no single AI lab should control the technology.

selectedTweets.text:
NEW: House Ag Chair GT Thompson said he’s not willing to “accept bad results” as a trade-off for the benefits of advancements in AI — a direct rebuttal to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

“As someone who practiced health care for 28 years, I’m never willing to accept bad results. I think we just need to do our best,” Thompson said, when I asked about Altman’s comments to @politico.

“We have to work harder to prevent any bad things from happening,” he added.

Altman told @BrendanBordelon that people “should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency.”

Read more: https://t.co/3Z1sOJ5Z21
